Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-v3-train-polish-0018", "row_sha256": "58d511ada5f7512b7b2cb0e299d9c058ad74e59ed7f7bc61edeff2fcc97793e9", "mode": "/polish", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Rewrite awkward phrasing into readable prose for the supplied profile, or plain prose when none is supplied. Preserve intent and certainty. Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "the cedar street community orchestra will have its spring concert on saturday, may 18, at 7:30 pm in the east hall at riverbend library. the doors are going to open at 7 pm. there is no charge to come in, and people can sit wherever there is an empty seat. the program includes the overture to the marriage of figaro by mozart, the second movement from dvořák’s new world symphony, and a new piece called harbor lights by local composer lena park. harbor lights is about six minutes long, and the orchestra will play it for the first time at this concert. the orchestra has 42 members, and its conductor is martin ellis. the concert is expected to last around 75 minutes, with no intermission. people who need an accessible entrance should use the library’s north doors, which have a ramp. parking is available in the library lot and on nearby streets, but the orchestra cannot reserve spaces. audience members are welcome to arrive early to choose seats. the library asks visitors not to bring food or drinks into the hall. the orchestra’s next open rehearsal is june 2 at 6:30 pm, also in the east hall; people may watch, but they should remain quiet while the musicians are playing.", "output": "The Cedar Street Community Orchestra will present its spring concert on Saturday, May 18, at 7:30 p.m. in the East Hall at Riverbend Library. Doors open at 7 p.m. Admission is free, and seating is available on a first-come, first-served basis.

The program includes Mozart’s Overture to The Marriage of Figaro, the second movement from Dvořák’s New World Symphony, and Harbor Lights, a new piece by local composer Lena Park. The orchestra will perform Harbor Lights, which is about six minutes long, for the first time at this concert.

The orchestra has 42 members and is conducted by Martin Ellis. The concert is expected to last about 75 minutes, with no intermission. Visitors who need an accessible entrance should use the library’s north doors, which have a ramp. Parking is available in the library lot and on nearby streets; the orchestra cannot reserve spaces. Audience members are welcome to arrive early to choose seats. The library asks visitors not to bring food or drinks into the hall.

The orchestra’s next open rehearsal is June 2 at 6:30 p.m., also in the East Hall. Visitors may watch, but should remain quiet while the musicians are playing."}]
